investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 16:26 and 16:34 UTC on 2026-08-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pods because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent (kata/peer-pods) workload in the production-api environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod the eval runner attempts to schedule is immediately rejected as Unschedulable, preventing agent creation from starting. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval checks for the remote-agents feature.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods (from prior eval runs, user workloads, or leaked pods from incomplete cleanup) are consuming all available VM slots, leaving none for new scheduling requests. Supported by all three checks reporting '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims found.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are fully occupied, any new pod is immediately unschedulable regardless of cluster-wide capacity.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup() wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) failed to delete prior eval pods, those pods would continue to hold VM resource slots and block new scheduling.

Lower confidence — a recent reduction in the number of kata/peer-pods-capable nodes (e.g., node drain, node failure, or scaling event) that reduced the eligible pool to 2 nodes with insufficient combined capacity.

investigations.summary: The model-matrix eval failed because exactly one of two configured models, aura-gpt-5-5, returned a 502 Bad Gateway wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable from the upstream LLM provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." The harness surfaced this as a 502 bad_gateway to the eval runner, causing the model result to record ok: false, provider: null, resolvedModel: null. This is an upstream provider availability failure localized to the aura-gpt-5-5 model route at the time of the eval run (2026-08-09T16:25:49.829Z–16:26:02.705Z). investigations.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 16:26 and 16:34 UTC on 2026-08-09 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pods because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner never received a VM ID or a remote state value, so all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent and the expected-output contract is fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent (kata/peer-pods) workload in the production-api environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. Every new remote-agent pod the eval runner attempts to schedule is immediately rejected as Unschedulable, preventing agent creation from starting. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet; the impact is currently scoped to the AURA observability eval checks for the remote-agents feature.

Supported by all three checks reporting '2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' with no preemption victims found.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch for 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, meaning the effective scheduling pool is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are fully occupied, any new pod is immediately unschedulable regardless of cluster-wide capacity.

Tertiary — leaked or stuck remote-agent pods from a previous eval run holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if the withCleanup() wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1883) failed to delete prior eval pods, those pods would continue to hold VM resource slots and block new scheduling.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-08-09T16:29–16:34Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place any new remote-agent pod because 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving 0/6 nodes available for scheduling.
